method: Static review: atomscan, cleave facts, PowerShell decryption, resolved CIL disassembly, rizin/capstone native control flow, and bounded Unicorn instruction emulation. No malware was run natively.

samples.marker_line: Blogger navbar: standard Google UI; fixed option/input mismatch
evidence: The base, canonical URL, WIZ configuration and relative static-script URL identify a BloggerNavbarUi frame, not the parent blog page.

The inline code installs browser polyfills, seals Object.prototype, deletes __proto__, collects UI timing, and routes UI events. It defines an XHR POST fallback for prototype-integrity reports to csp.withgoogle.com; the supplied deleteIsEnforced and sealIsEnforced settings skip its heartbeat and periodic integrity-reporting branches.

The form is a GET search of the blog. The absolute URL value incorrectly attributed to an input is an option in the sharing/reporting menu. The Basic Base64 string decodes to static bootstrap credential material, not executable code or collected secrets.

No stealing, deceptive credential collection, destructive behavior or backdoor was established in the saved bytes. The verdict is limited to this navigation frame; no deployment or parent-page safety is assumed.

samples.identification: AES/XOR PowerShell loader with managed process hollowing
samples.marker_line: PowerShell image loader: encrypted stages hollow a native host
evidence: The outer wrapper Base64-decodes an embedded payload and AES-256-CBC/PKCS7-decrypts it, creates a ScriptBlock from the UTF-8 result and immediately invokes it.

The recovered script Base64-decodes, applies a repeating UTF-8 XOR key, Base64-decodes the result again, loads the resulting managed assembly and invokes FILE.WHORE.LAUNCHER with a Framework aspnet_compiler.exe path and a separate MZ byte array.

The launcher CIL creates a process with 0x08000004 flags, reads saved context and PEB image base, unmaps when needed, allocates remote RWX memory, writes PE headers and sections, replaces PEB.ImageBaseAddress, sets CONTEXT.Eax to replacement base plus entry RVA, sets context and resumes the thread.
The script polls host liveness every five seconds and relaunches when absent. The name Start-BeaconCycle does not establish a network beacon.

The replacement PE has importless, high-entropy code and an indexed byte-XOR/store helper. Static disassembly and bounded instruction emulation did not recover a final named payload or establish theft/C2 behavior.

Encrypted staging plus concealed reflective loading and replacement-image execution in an unrelated native host tip the judgment to malicious. No legitimate authorized-test provenance was supplied; no final-payload family or runtime success is asserted.

samples.identification: Damaged StormAttack service/DLL injector and installer
samples.marker_line: StormAttack injector: Active Setup, service hijack, self-delete
evidence: Entry 0x402674 calls 0x401cb0; configuration DWORD at 0x404120 is 3, selecting Active Setup and self-copy code.

At 0x401900 the program makes a GUID, sets HKLM Active Setup Installed Components StubPath to a Windows-directory copy, reads and patches its own image, writes the copy and launches it. Fixed patch offsets do not map cleanly to the current configuration field, so successful mode changes are not assumed.
At 0x401150 it creates a hidden host process, allocates remote memory for a DLL path, writes it, resolves LoadLibraryA and passes that export as CreateRemoteThread entry.

At 0x401260 it deletes and replaces LanmanServer Parameters ServiceDLL. Other configuration branches copy its image, set Hidden|System attributes (6), create an auto-start service (start type 2) and start it.
At 0x401390 it uses its own short module path with COMSPEC /c del for cleanup. The DLL path, DDoS server/welcome banners and injector targets support StormAttack identity.

The resource section is entirely zeroed. Resource APIs and extraction/injection code survive, but no embedded DLL was recovered and successful payload installation is not asserted. There is no static evidence of WannaCry or file encryption.
System-service hijacking together with hidden persistence, injection and cleanup tips the judgment to malicious despite damaged packaging. No authorized deployment context is known.

changes: Require input-tag context and real type/value attribute names, ignore HTML comments, and describe URL declaration without claiming visible display. This removes the real Blogger option false positive and the corresponding synthetic phishing-consumer near miss; URL input and real submit-form coverage remain.

Consolidate the duplicate Closure copyright matcher under its existing library identity, extend that atom to HTML, and update exact consumers. No application identity is inferred solely from a copied library header. Ancestor app selectors no longer acquire that header as application evidence.

Move the AES script-wrapper execution rule into execution/payload/script-eval, preserving its matcher, criticality and effective scope; preserve its former directory-consumer membership through an exact reference. Describe required co-occurrence without claiming proven crypto-to-eval flow.

Add notable object sealing, browser beacon/navigator-binding initialization, and x86 indexed XOR/store loop observations. No sample-specific hostname, mask key, chosen filename, campaign name or exact file size is required.

controls.outside_batch_legitimate_url_input: testdata/clickfix-startmenu-paste/execcommand-only-near-miss.html retains html-input-url-value with no hostile/suspicious findings

closure_reference.result: Canonical library identity retained; duplicate app header finding removed; no hostile/suspicious losses across decoded units.

controls.phishing_consumer: Actual input-submit form matches before and after; unrelated option URL beside a submit input matches only before.

limitations: No authorized deployment context or publisher provenance was provided for either loader.
The native PE has no recoverable resources; no ransomware, successful installation, live C2 or final DDoS action is inferred.
The PowerShell final PE remains packed; no stealer family, final C2 endpoint, successful theft or persistence beyond the script lifetime is claimed.
The input-tag matcher is bounded to 999 preceding attribute bytes because this engine does not expose an HTML tree-sitter grammar.
The engine-emitted percent-decoding of the StormAttack GUID printf format is not a YAML claim; it is not a network URL. No shadow YAML exception was introduced.
The provided Triage URL was inaccessible; verdicts rely on surviving code and bytes.
Atomscan reports feature-spec v18 while the engine expects v21. Local before/after comparisons used the same model and scan settings.
final_required_check: make validate (run after this review and marker generation)
